scope.equations: unforced incompressible Navier-Stokes with no-slip u^nu=0 on bounded C^2 domain; smooth incompressible Euler with U.n=0
scope.time: fixed [0,T] on which classical Euler solution exists
scope.data: strongest baseline uses one common L2 initial datum for every nu

claims.statement: For each fixed c>0, strong convergence u^nu->U in L-infinity(0,T;L2(Omega)) is equivalent to nu integral_0^T integral_{dist(x,boundary)<c nu} |grad u^nu|^2 -> 0, for Leray-Hopf no-slip solutions with common initial data equal to a classical Euler datum and no forcing.

quantifiers.domain: bounded C^2 Omega subset R^d, d=2 or 3
quantifiers.time: every fixed T within classical Euler lifespan
quantifiers.solutions: any Leray-Hopf solution family with fixed u0 and no-slip trace
quantifiers.strip: one fixed c>0 suffices; convergence forces the condition for every fixed c>0

claims.cost: No asymptotic computational cost. Corrector support thickness c nu; norms are L2 O(sqrt(nu)), gradient L2 O(nu^-1/2), gradient Linfinity O(nu^-1).
claims.falsifier: A solution family meeting the interface assumptions with Kato-strip dissipation tending to zero but nonvanishing strong L-infinity_t L2_x error. This would contradict the stated theorem.

claims.statement: The Kato corrector and relative-energy argument gives sup_{t<=T} (1/2)||u^nu(t)-U(t)||_2^2 <= exp(2 M T)[(1/2)||u0^nu-U0||_2^2 + C(nu^(1/2)+D_K^nu+sqrt(D_K^nu))], with M=||grad U||_L-infinity and C independent of nu.

quantifiers.corrector: divergence free, support in fixed c nu strip, trace U on wall
quantifiers.C_dependencies: Omega, c, T, fixed Euler norms, uniform initial L2 bound

claims.cost: Residual terms: corrector endpoints/time derivative O(sqrt(nu)); corrector convection O(D_K); viscous corrector cross term O(sqrt(D_K)); Euler viscous cross term O(sqrt(nu)).
claims.falsifier: An algebraic/sign error in the weak test U-v^nu or a corrector violating one of the displayed norm/trace/support assumptions.

claims.statement: The Leray-Hopf energy inequality yields only D_K^nu<=||u0||_2^2/2 and therefore does not itself prove D_K^nu->0. A uniform-in-nu L-infinity_t H1 bound does imply D_K^nu<=C T nu->0.

quantifiers.energy_bound: fixed common initial datum and unforced flow
quantifiers.enstrophy_sufficient_bound: sup_{nu,t<=T} ||grad u^nu(t)||_2^2 <= C_E independent of nu

claims.cost: D_K<=nu times the full enstrophy integral; a bound C nu^-alpha with alpha<1 suffices, while alpha=1 gives O(1).
claims.falsifier: The stated inequalities are direct consequences of energy/enstrophy bounds; a stronger conclusion from energy alone would need an additional PDE estimate not assumed here.

claims.statement: For smooth no-slip Navier-Stokes flow, the kinetic energy in the strip dist<delta obeys the exact integrated local balance with viscous loss nu integral |grad u|^2 and signed flux through the inner interface Sigma_delta; physical-wall flux vanishes.

quantifiers.forcing: unforced; force term is stated separately in RESULT.txt

claims.cost: None beyond integration of the local kinetic-energy identity.
claims.falsifier: Differentiate the displayed flux; it must yield u dot Delta u + |grad u|^2.

claims.statement: The exact channel shear u^nu=(e^{nu t Delta_D}1,0) converges uniformly in time in L2 to stationary Euler U=(1,0); its Kato-strip dissipation is O(nu(1+log_+(T/nu))) while its enstrophy is not uniformly bounded.

quantifiers.data: v(y,0)=1 in L2 for all nu

claims.cost: Fourier heat-series solution; no numerics. Kato estimate C nu(1+log_+(T/nu)).
claims.falsifier: Direct substitution into heat equation/boundary values or a corrected half-line heat-kernel estimate.

claims.statement: This leaf does not construct an actual equal-data unforced Navier-Stokes family violating the Kato condition; a February 2026 NoDEA article reports that no rigorous violation was known to its authors as of publication.

quantifiers.claim_scope: authors' literature-status statement; no priority or universal impossibility claim

claims.cost: Bounded source review through the cited 2026 article; no exhaustive search or expert review.
claims.falsifier: A rigorous counterexample published or available before the cited article's cutoff, or a later construction.

claims.statement: Resolving the Kato strip on a uniform d-dimensional mesh needs h<=O(nu) and asymptotically h/nu->0; at h~nu this is O(nu^-d) cells and an explicit step size O(nu), hence O(nu^-(d+1)) cell updates over fixed T.

quantifiers.assumptions: fixed nondimensional domain and O(1) characteristic speed

claims.cost: No actual mesh or computation used.
claims.falsifier: A specified discretization with a proved coarser-layer resolution guarantee or different stability/CFL restriction.

primary proof source for a density-dependent extension; homogeneous case recovers Kato; Section 1 includes the bounded statement that no rigorous Kato violation was known to the authors
